dedupe_keys.name: cross crowd simulation of situated individuals a festival crowd model

description: CROSS, Crowd Simulation of Situated individuals, is a simulation for understanding crowd behaviour as a social scientific tool. Each person in the crowd is a social-cognitive agent affected by the social and physical surroundings, and behaviour patterns emerge at group level from the links between what goes on inside and between individuals. The model adds a cognitive level of behaviour to crowd research and uses simulation experiments to test theory, applied here to a festival crowd. It was published by Nanda Wijermans on CoMSES in 2011, with release 1.1.0 in April 2013. Coverage: a stylised festival site. Access: free Repast code on CoMSES. Licence: GPL-2.0. Caveats: an older model built for theory testing, not for operational crowd management. Simulation uses are exploring crowd dynamics and safety at events in public spaces. Related records: the BNE pedestrian evacuation model and the evolutionary game crowd evacuation model.
inputs: Social-cognitive agent states and group membership
name: CROSS: crowd simulation of situated individuals, a festival crowd model
outputs: Emergent crowd behaviour patterns at group level
